maya: Heads-up — planning to add a route rule that respects the `X-Model-Pin` header for partner traffic. Need to think through compatibility and quotas.

sam: Do we want to let customers pin to any alias? risk: incompatible quantized variants could crash serving path.

kevin: We should require a compatibility check or version constraint. e.g. if header present: verify alias maps to a compatible runtime. Example rule: `if header X-Model-Pin then allow_pin=true && require_compat>=major`

liz: UX note — console should surface "pinned by header" on rollout page and add telemetry so we can see pinned vs normal traffic.

ryan: Quota/ops thought: pinned requests may bypass multi-model batching and spike GPU usage. suggest per-route qps cap for header-pinned traffic.

maya: Proposed route config (sketch):
```
routes:
  - match: path: "/v1/generate"
    headers:
      x-model-pin: present
    action: pin_alias
    header_pin: true
    require_compat: ">=1.2"
    quota: 1000
```

sam: Prefer explicit flags like `allow_header_pin: true` + `compatibility_policy: "reject" | "fallback"` so behavior isn't implicit.

kevin: Fallback idea: try a compatible quantized variant (eg `open-llama-7b.q4_0`) when exact alias is incompatible, but emit telemetry `was_fallback:true` and include which variant used.

liz: :thumbsup: telemetry flags are critical. we'll add a dashboard tile for "header-pinned traffic" and a gauge for "fallback rate".

maya: Edge case — enterprise customers might pin to internal names we don't map. behaviour: reject with 400 and return allowed-aliases list (no silent fallback).

ryan: Ops: add alert when pinned traffic >20% of route and p99 latency increases >30% vs baseline.

sam: Also ensure rollout UX shows when a header-pin overrides canary. I think default should be "pin bypasses rollout" unless route config sets `honor_rollout: true`.

kevin: Agreed. Default `honor_rollout=false` for header pins and require opt-in. Otherwise pins defeat staged rollouts.

maya: I'll open a PR for the new route schema + compatibility checks, then a console follow-up for telemetry. assigning to @kevin and @liz for review.

deploy-bot: PR created: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4821 by maya — needs review

liz: I'll review this afternoon. small ask: add a unit test that sets `route.pin_source=header` and asserts metric labels.

sam: And add an e2e that triggers an incompatible alias and asserts `fallback_count` increments when policy is fallback.

maya: Cool — thanks. i'll wire up the schema and tests next
